summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, right flank pain, and cloudy urine, concerning for pyelonephritis and urosepsis, eight days after discharge from a prior admission for ileal conduit urinary diversion. He had leukocytosis, acute kidney injury, and imaging showed bilateral hydronephrosis. Urine cultures grew Enterococcus species, including VRE, prompting addition of daptomycin to meropenem. He initially refused some antibiotic doses, but psychiatry confirmed he had capacity to make that decision. His infection resolved, with improvement in white count and renal function. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotics. He was discharged home with visiting nurse services to complete a 12-day course of meropenem and 7-day course of daptomycin, along with instructions for low-potassium diet and close follow-up.
